description.text: Law is a discipline that takes legal phenomena and their laws as its research object, aiming to systematically explain legal principles, norms and practices, and cultivate professional talents with legal thinking, practical ability and a sense of social justice. As an interdisciplinary field of social sciences and humanities, law not only involves the interpretation of legal provisions (such as the Constitution and the Civil Code), but also covers the value logic behind the law (such as fairness and justice), social functions (such as rights protection and order maintenance), and historical evolution (such as the influence of Roman law on modern rule of law). The major emphasizes the integration of theory and practice, serving areas such as legislation, judiciary, law enforcement, and legal services. It is a core supporting discipline in a modern society ruled by law.

duration.text: The Law at Sun Yat-sen University is a 3 Years long program for international students, taught in Chinese.

requirements.text: (1) Non-Chinese citizens holding valid foreign passports.(2) Be in good physical and mental health and meet the physical examination standards for applying for a study visa or residence permit to China.(3) Those who come to China to pursue a master's degree must have a degree equivalent to a bachelor's degree from a Chinese university and be no older than 35 years old. Those who come to China to pursue a doctoral degree must have a degree equivalent to a master's degree from a Chinese university and be no older than 40 years old.(4) Be friendly to China, diligent and eager to learn, have excellent academic performance, good conduct, abide by laws and regulations, have no record of violating school rules and regulations, no public security penalties, and no criminal records.(5) Language ProficiencyFor those applying for master's or doctoral degrees in Chinese-taught programs, their Chinese proficiency must reach 180 points or above on the HSK5 level of the Chinese Proficiency Test. To apply for the Master's degree in Teaching Chinese to Speakers of Other Languages, one must achieve a score of 210 or above in HSK5 and 60 or above in the Intermediate level of HSKK. Applicants who have used Chinese as the medium of instruction can submit a "Certificate of Teaching in Chinese" issued by their school. After being recognized by our school, they can be exempted from submitting the HSK score certificate.For applications to English-taught programs, if the native language is not English, one must submit proof of TOEFL (TOEFL iBT score of 79 or above, with 15 or above in each section) or IELTS (IELTS Academic score of 6.5 or above, with 5.5 or above in each section) or other proof that can reflect one's English proficiency. Applicants who have used English as the medium of instruction can submit a "Certificate of English Teaching" issued by their school. After being recognized by our school, they will be exempted from submitting the certificate of English proficiency.
